required_plan: Customer-controlled containers, PostgreSQL 18, and either private S3-compatible, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob object storage. Platform-native workload identity and secret injection are recommended.

atomic_store.notes: PostgreSQL transactions atomically persist the message, recipient ledger, idempotency claim, and deterministic outbox intent.

recipient_ledger.notes: PostgreSQL is the provider-neutral authority for messages, recipients, attempts, immutable events, and outbox state.

payload_store.notes: One attachment port supports private S3-compatible, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob stores with signed direct uploads, declared checksum metadata, size verification, and final byte-level SHA-256 validation.

queue_wakeup.notes: PostgreSQL jobs remain authoritative and provide deterministic identities, ordered SKIP LOCKED leases, bounded retries, expired-lease recovery, and terminal failure isolation. Cloud Run can add a content-free Pub/Sub REST pull hint with split publisher/subscriber identities; publish, pull, acknowledgment, duplicate, or retention failure never changes durable job truth.

scheduler_wakeup.notes: PostgreSQL due times retain the 30-day contract independently of optional immediate-work wake-up accelerators; hosted long-delay and redeploy evidence remains pending.

periodic_reconciliation.notes: Every worker periodically reconciles committed outbox rows and due jobs, recovering after process or wake-up loss.

secret_injection.notes: Bootstrap API and PostgreSQL secrets accept mutually exclusive environment or bounded absolute mounted-file injection; storage SDKs use provider workload identity and credential chains.

provider_event_ingress.notes: ACS Event Grid and SendGrid Signed Event Webhook ingresses authenticate independently, validate provider schemas, and apply exact recipient delivery reports; hosted lifecycle evidence remains pending.

webhook_egress.notes: Durable PostgreSQL jobs deliver signed webhooks through public-endpoint validation and bounded privacy-safe retries.

backup_restore.notes: PostgreSQL plus object-store backup and isolated restore evidence is still required for every deployment pack.

safe_deploy.notes: The pinned Cloud Run, Render, Railway, and Fly.io packs use migration-first rollouts and immutable images; hosted lifecycle proof and the remaining platform packs are still required.

doctor.notes: Readiness verifies applied PostgreSQL migrations and the selected object-storage container, but platform identity, retention, encryption, and lifecycle policy checks remain open.

upgrade.notes: Forward-only additive migrations are checksum-pinned and advisory-lock serialized; exact platform rollout evidence remains open.

rollback.notes: Application rollback can retain compatible schema and object state, but each platform pack requires an isolated rollback drill.

cleanup.notes: No portable platform pack has yet published zero-residue cleanup evidence.

sources.title: Google Cloud Storage V4 signed URLs

limitations: The runtime remains experimental until one exact platform deployment passes lifecycle, backup/restore, terminal delivery, controlled receipt, and zero-residue cleanup evidence.
Direct-upload metadata binds the declared SHA-256 to the signed upload contract; HayaSend additionally re-hashes downloaded bytes immediately before provider submission.
Inbound receiving remains disabled; provider-event ingress is currently implemented for ACS Email and SendGrid only.
